matched_denominator_policy: only cases answered in BOTH arms enter any cross-arm comparison; answerable and unanswerable are reported on their own matched sets and never pooled

arm_b_explicit_unknown.note: selecting insufficient_evidence on an answerable case is WRONG, not partial credit

arm_C_external_threshold_sweep.definition: act iff p(ground-truth option) >= threshold; arm A's own requests, no new API calls

arm_B_explicit_unknown_sweep.definition: abstain iff p(insufficient_evidence) >= threshold; the like-for-like operating curve against arm C
arm_B_explicit_unknown_sweep.grid: full range 0.000-1.000 at 0.001, plus the 0.01 reporting grid

arm_a_forced.note: provider confidence is a DERIVED function of the probability vector (Phase 1 INSTRUMENT-VALIDATION) and is not independent evidence

arm_b_explicit_unknown.note: provider confidence is a DERIVED function of the probability vector (Phase 1 INSTRUMENT-VALIDATION) and is not independent evidence

measured_calibration_descriptive.claim: NONE. n is far too small for a reliability claim; this is a descriptive binning computed by us, not the provider's, and it is not evidence that Jev is calibrated.

headline.verdict: EXPLICIT UNKNOWN WINS on the matched comparison. At its best zero-false-unknown operating point it detects 10/10 unanswerable cases (1.0) while flagging none of the 57 answerable ones, versus the external threshold's best 0.9 at 0.6667 answerable coverage. NOTE the argmax selection rate is only 0.3; the probability-based operating point is far better than the option the model actually selects.
